metadata.case_name: LI TING FAI v. WOO CHI KEUNG

injuries.description: whiplash injury to the neck resulting in neck pain and stiffness
source: This is a whiplash neck injury case.
The Plaintiff was diagnosed by Dr. Chan to have a whiplash injury to the neck resulting in neck pain and stiffness.
injuries.icd_description: Acute whiplash associated disorder with complaint of neck pain, stiffness or tenderness only

manifestations.description: paraesthesia down the right arm to involve the hand
numbness of right upper limb / right little finger numbness
trouble sleeping / insomnia (woken by pain and numbness)
worsening hypersensitivity status with easy and frequent occurrence of generalized and extensive rashes

treatments_received: MRI scan of the cervical spine
admitted to St. Paul's Hospital on 28/9/05 and discharged on 29/9/05
treatments_future: hospitalisation for continuous neck traction for a period of 2 weeks
analgesics and anti-inflammatory medications including steroid injections

losses.description: Residual neck pain and stiffness resulting from whiplash injury to the neck

comparable_cases.injury_description: whiplash injury to the neck, contusion to the forehead and face, and possible contusion of the anterior left shin. There was residual neck pain and the Plaintiff was advised to practise regular neck and postural exercise and pay attention to her neck at work and at leisure. She received 11 sessions of physiotherapy treatments.

struck the head by an object and was knocked unconscious for 2 hours. He suffered post-concussional syndrome with symptoms of headaches and dizziness. He suffered soft tissue injuries and loss of lordotic curvature of his cervical spine and mild neck pain subsisting.

whiplash injury with deep lacerated wound on her right forehead and 2 small lacerated wounds over her mid-forehead. She had a swollen eye and was unable to open her eyelids due to periorbital haematoma. She had residual neck pain and muscle spasm.
whiplash injury with soft tissue injury; plaintiff suffered post-accident limitations including reduced ability to play tennis and persistent neck symptoms.
whiplash neck injury with soft tissue injury, persistent neck pain and weakness on upper limbs for about a year. He was granted sick leave for 2 years.
sprained neck injury; hospitalized same day and discharged 2 days later; received physiotherapy for more than 3 months; intermittent residual neck pain.
